experiments.scope: The exact sha3-256-r5-prefix-v1 target. Once per run the program checks its 5-round SHA3-256 against two known-answer digests of the organizer reference and its 24-round version against hashlib.sha3_256, rank 40 of W40 and the 780 two-round polarizations of Lemma 3. The 256 trials form one group: trial k is lane c = k of the cosets j = 256h + c of proof.md Section 6.1 (h = int(seed of trial 0, 16) mod G); the counted leader step draws the origin of coset j from two coin words of trial k (SHA-256 of its seed and a counter, a reproducible stand-in for fresh coins). The group executes the schedule of proof.md Sections 5 to 7 at reduced size (the first 2^9 Gray points of each coset, all 175 planes, the full 140-bit key, the sparse-set table with arbitrary initial sparse words, native verification of key matches) through a counting machine and stops unless every executed count equals the formula of proof.md. Premise test (proof.md Section 12.2): trial k returns the first two of the 512 Gray points of its own coset whose digests agree on the 16 masked bits (bits 0..3 of digest lanes 0..3), found from the emitted keys and checked natively. Different trials use disjoint message sets.
experiments.hypothesis: Reduced-width form of premise H_coset on the trials' own random-origin digests. If digests of distinct messages behave as independent uniform values on these 16 bits, a set of 512 contains an agreeing pair with probability P = 1 - prod_{i<512} (1 - i/2^16) = 0.864841510863844, so the organizer-recomputed successes of the 256 trials follow Binomial(256, P): expectation 221.40, standard deviation 5.47, pass interval [200, 243] (expectation +- 4 sd). A mask success is a 16-bit partial match, not a collision. The program also stops unless the group's exact pair counts lie in their pass intervals (expectation +- 4 sd; Var = n p (1 - p), pair indicators of uniform values being pairwise independent): pairs16_within, two points of one coset agreeing on key bits 0..15 (n = 33,488,896 pairs, expectation 511), in [421, 601]; pairs16_cross, points of two different cosets agreeing on bits 0..15 (n = 8,556,380,160, expectation 130,560), in [129115, 132005]; pairs24_cross, the same on bits 0..23 (expectation 510), in [420, 600]. The other observations are the executed operation counts of proof.md Section 13. Scope: 2^17 digests of one group, 16- and 24-bit projections, 9-dimensional sub-cosets; nothing about 256-bit rates or cost is inferred from the run.

experiments.scope: The same program, target, checks, group and reduced schedule as experiment hcoset-within16 (proof.md Sections 5 to 7 and 13), on the organizer seeds of this experiment, hence an independent group of 256 random-origin cosets. Premise test (proof.md Section 12.2): trial k returns the first Gray point b >= 256 of the partner coset (lane c XOR 1, an independent origin) whose digest agrees on the 16 masked bits (bits 0..3 of digest lanes 0..3) with a Gray point a < 256 of its own coset, and that a, found from the emitted keys and checked natively. Different trials use disjoint message sets: points 0..255 of their own coset and points 256..511 of the partner coset.
experiments.hypothesis: Reduced-width form of premise H_coset across cosets with independent uniform origins. If digests of distinct messages behave as independent uniform values on these 16 bits, two disjoint sets of 256 contain an agreeing cross pair with probability P = 0.632121969489614 (exact, from the occupancy law of one set), so the organizer-recomputed successes of the 256 trials follow Binomial(256, P): expectation 161.82, standard deviation 7.72, pass interval [131, 192] (expectation +- 4 sd). A mask success is a 16-bit partial match, not a collision. The program also stops unless the group's exact pair counts lie in the pass intervals stated for experiment hcoset-within16: pairs16_within in [421, 601], pairs16_cross in [129115, 132005], pairs24_cross in [420, 600]. Scope: 2^17 digests of one group, 16- and 24-bit projections, 9-dimensional sub-cosets; nothing about 256-bit rates or cost is inferred from the run.
